title: Degree-zero homogeneous localization
statement:
Let $R=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}R_n$ be an $\mathbb N$-graded commutative ring and
let $f\in R$. Write $R_{(f),0}$ for the degree-zero part of the homogeneous
localization of $R$ away from $f$. Its elements are represented by

$$
\frac{x}{f^m},\qquad m\geq0,\quad x\in R_e,\quad f^m\in R_e
\text{ for some } e,
$$

modulo the ordinary localization relation in $R_f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. When $f\in R_d$ these are the
fractions $x/f^m$ with $x\in R_{md}$.

mathlib_match.how: exact: specialize the grading index to ℕ. Away (line 601) is HomogeneousLocalization at Submonoid.powers f, with no homogeneity hypothesis on f. NumDenSameDeg (line 96) requires numerator and denominator in one common component; HomogeneousLocalization (line 281) is its quotient by the kernel of embedding (line 270) into the ordinary localization. Thus its representatives are exactly x/f^m with x and f^m in R_e. The constructor HomogeneousLocalization.mk (line 292) and mk_surjective (line 295) supply all such representatives; val_mk (line 305) and val_injective (line 312) identify equality with equality in R_f. For homogeneous f ∈ R_d, Away.mk (line 609), Away.val_mk (line 613) and Away.mk_surjective (line 618) give exactly x ∈ R_(m*d), with n • d = n*d for ℕ. No positivity or regularity hypothesis is needed, including nilpotent f.
